I am a PhD student at Rutgers University's School of Communication and
Information, working with Kiran Garimella. My current project follows
misinformation as it moves through private messaging platforms — encrypted,
hard to instrument, and increasingly the dominant medium of political talk
in much of the world. A second strand, supported by the Security, Trust &
Safety Initiative at Cornell Tech, traces the organization of hate-speech
campaigns through the 2016 Philippine elections on Facebook.

Before Rutgers I read computational social science at the University of
Chicago, where I worked with Molly Offer-Westort and Nick Feamster on
adaptive field-experimental tools for correcting misperceptions on Indian
WhatsApp. Earlier still I was an engineer — embedded firmware at Bosch, a
brief turn co-founding a small water-monitoring startup, and an undergraduate
stint on the BITS Pilani Hyperloop pod team.
